title: What The Bagpipes Know (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 98bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal Scottish Celtic philosophy absurdist heritage
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The bagpipes were weaponised at the Battle of Waterloo
A piper led the troops in because someone felt it's what you do
The English banned the bagpipes for a time as an instrument of war
Which tells you something about what the bagpipes are for

[Pre-Chorus]
My grandfather played them on a hillside in Argyll
I inherited the memory and nothing else — that's my style

[Chorus]
What do the bagpipes know that I don't know?
They know that every funeral gets better with the drone below
What do the bagpipes know on a Scottish hill?
They know the sound of grief and joy are both the same until
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The chanter is the melody, the drones are the foundation
Three drones going constantly beneath your entire nation
You cannot play the bagpipes quietly — this is by design
The bagpipes have no volume setting and that suits them fine

[Bridge]
Someone always cries at bagpipes — this is universal law
No matter who you are or where you're from or what you saw
The sound bypasses reason and goes straight to something older
Before the clan, before the name, before the order

[Outro]
Bagpipes know… older than the argument… bagpipes know
Scotland knows — that's my boy
